# dsh-SIWC

Sign in with ChatGPT on deepseek harness

The current package is `@f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0-alpha.5`, published on npm under the `alpha` dist-tag, with source and setup guidance in [`packages/chatgpt`](packages/chatgpt/README.md). The preserved v5 artifact under the former identity `@f4ah6o/dsh-chatgpt@0.1.0` is historical only. This repository has no build-time dependency on a sibling DeepSeek Harness checkout.

The package declares compatibility with the DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.1` through `0.2.1-alpha.4`, and `0.2.1-rc.2` API lines and their corresponding Cordis runtimes. Its build uses the published Typert generator with the narrow pinned patch in [`patches`](patches); the package tests check the generated Host Remote contract and OAuth lifecycle, while `pnpm run build` also builds the lazy Client entry point.

Run `pnpm install`, `pnpm run build`, and `pnpm test` from this directory. Profile requirements, account setup, headless browser sign-in, and model configuration are in the [package README](packages/chatgpt/README.md). Release operators can follow the [npm publishing guide](PUBLISHING.md).

## Install from npm

Install the published prerelease into an initialized Desktop profile with Desktop's managed `dsh` command (fully quit Desktop first):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0-alpha.5
```

The published `0.1.0-alpha.4` does not accept DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` in its compatibility range, so use `0.1.0-alpha.5` for the current DSH line. Use Desktop's bundled CLI or Plugin Manager, not an npm-installed `dsh` command. If the profile has the former package installed, fully quit Desktop and remove it before installing the renamed package:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove @f4ah6o/dsh-chatgpt
```

Do not keep both package names in one profile. The historical v5 artifact is [`@f4ah6o/dsh-chatgpt@0.1.0`](dist/f4ah6o-dsh-chatgpt-0.1.0.tgz), SHA-256 `66ed59d58fe7d241d2cfcfc777939a7a3d7d49710cdce4cbecc9dcee8ffeeb2d`; it is an ignored, untracked workspace file. The prior prepublication `0.1.0` candidate is [`@f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0`](dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0.tgz), SHA-256 `15c16502dc658f752c5551b116d98dae286f32c69de3cc9e4d54a279ef1c4110`; its official and fork consumer matrix passed for that exact tarball. The published `0.1.0-alpha.5` artifact is [`@f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0-alpha.5`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@f12o/dsh-siwc/v/0.1.0-alpha.5), registry SHA-256 `9ca8b408d0336423aa02f25a1bdf8df39e67678d6b0dbc7bc153d2152dba3c55`, SHA-1 `f16d3aa8adae1e67183fbbb26d0a4f99b5fce1e2`, integrity `sha512-hlmoJgvXyIKMS+Bmp0eNY/63/RPjJ1xvrt5nIHJz6Z6ltsaB3UdCpm3QABPnO4CJzfYqxcVNezydGBO0w7y3RA==`; it was built and published with provenance by [workflow run 39027790810](https://github.com/f4ah6o/dsh-SIWC/actions/runs/39027790810). The local candidate tarball is [`dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0-alpha.5.tgz`](dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0-alpha.5.tgz), SHA-256 `7425bc6ed094e2c9e560b9d9700bb204271f7e37fd2a126bfa9c2df08ea10039`; it is an ignored, untracked workspace file. Both the local candidate and the registry artifact passed the build, typecheck, and 75-test suite, the auxiliary wire probe against published DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` packages, and an installed Web smoke on the current `0.2.1-rc.2` runtime, where the Host Remote loaded and the ChatGPT settings section rendered the empty-account state. No live ChatGPT inference was performed for this release. The earlier [`@f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0-alpha.1`](dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0-alpha.1.tgz) tarball, SHA-256 `3c5f83e28a590c804245d05791b5cbead7fbbcc400649ed861bf775c02524a02`, remains historical. The [alpha artifact comparison](validation/alpha-artifact-proof.json) records that the alpha.1 and `0.1.0` tarballs differ in the three package READMEs, the version-only manifest change, and generated CSS-map property ordering in `lib/client.js`; the CSS maps have the same key/value pairs. Desktop acceptance remains pending. A Windows Desktop attempt with official DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` failed after plugin installation because `ctx.connection` was missing when Desktop read `authenticatedUrl`; the underlying composition cause is unresolved. See the [verification report](validation/fork-verification.md) and [installed-Desktop checklist](validation/desktop-verification.md).

## Validation artifacts

- [Japanese package setup](packages/chatgpt/README.ja.md)
- Prior prepublication candidate: [`@f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0`](dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0.tgz), ignored and untracked; its SHA-256 is `15c16502dc658f752c5551b116d98dae286f32c69de3cc9e4d54a279ef1c4110`.
- Published alpha: [`@f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0-alpha.5`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@f12o/dsh-siwc/v/0.1.0-alpha.5), registry SHA-256 `9ca8b408d0336423aa02f25a1bdf8df39e67678d6b0dbc7bc153d2152dba3c55`, SHA-1 `f16d3aa8adae1e67183fbbb26d0a4f99b5fce1e2`; build, typecheck, 75 tests, the auxiliary wire probe, and an installed Web smoke passed on DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`.
- Local alpha candidate: [`dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0-alpha.5.tgz`](dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0-alpha.5.tgz), SHA-256 `7425bc6ed094e2c9e560b9d9700bb204271f7e37fd2a126bfa9c2df08ea10039`; ignored and untracked, kept as the pre-publication validation artifact.
- Historical alpha tarball: [`@f12o/dsh-siwc@0.1.0-alpha.1`](dist/f12o-dsh-siwc-0.1.0-alpha.1.tgz), SHA-256 `3c5f83e28a590c804245d05791b5cbead7fbbcc400649ed861bf775c02524a02`; its earlier CLI/SDK/Web smoke matrix passed on official DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`, official `0.2.1-alpha.1`, and the then-current fork.
- [Alpha artifact comparison](validation/alpha-artifact-proof.json) — content comparison of the alpha.1 and prior `0.1.0` tarballs.
- Historical v5 tarball: [`@f4ah6o/dsh-chatgpt@0.1.0`](dist/f4ah6o-dsh-chatgpt-0.1.0.tgz), ignored and untracked; it may be absent in a fresh clone and is not the current package identity.
- [Fork verification report](validation/fork-verification.md)
- [Pending installed-Desktop verification checklist](validation/desktop-verification.md)

plugins.description: Persistent agent memory for DeepSeek Harness: daily journals, Dream consolidation, weekly reviews and verified cross-session recall.
plugins.readme_text:
# Dream & Memory for DeepSeek Harness

[简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) · [Security](SECURITY.md)

Turn verified DSH conversations into **daily journals, Dream consolidations, weekly reviews, and searchable long-term memory**, without loading whole conversations into every prompt.

## Incremental Dream consolidation

Dream processes up to seven new or modified managed daily journals per run (looking back at most 30 days), including securely archived daily copies. It never rescans the raw transcript as part of routine consolidation. Source-backed candidate extraction and task tracking remain with the daily pipeline; a Dream model output containing fabricated facts or task events is rejected.

Successful complete model batches are cached in derived SQLite for up to seven days; model transport failures can retry once and unfinished work remains eligible for the next run. The model request cancellation budget is 120 seconds and the overall consolidation cancellation budget is eight minutes. No new journals means no model call. Successful daily analysis advances its source cursor even if some candidate facts are rejected; model failure does not advance that cursor.

## Memory lifecycle

1. **Daily journal:** summarize eligible user messages into `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`.
2. **Dream:** incrementally consolidate new or updated daily journals into `DREAMS.md` without rescanning raw conversations or fabricating candidate evidence.
3. **Long-term memory:** verify source evidence and publish approved facts to managed sections of `MEMORY.md`.
4. **Recall:** fetch a few relevant published facts from the current authorized workspace; optional embeddings complement keyword search.
5. **Weekly review:** merge the previous week's daily journals, track coverage, and safely archive eligible daily files.

The original native DSH session log remains the evidence source. Candidate memories are not automatically treated as facts, and retrieved user content is not trusted as instructions.

## Semantic recall and historical archives

Automatic recall of **verified, source-backed long-term memory** can use keyword, semantic-fallback, or hybrid matching (`autoRecallMode`). Embedding failures fall back to lexical retrieval; content from unverified history never enters trusted automatic recall.

The single read-only `memory_search` model tool supports `action: 'search'` (default, compatible with existing queries) and `action: 'topics'` (the verified topic index). The plugin maintains a scoped, incremental SQLite index for explicit `memory_search` over curated archives under `memory/history/{daily,weekly,monthly,notes}/`. Only these structured Markdown paths are scanned; account/configuration files and migrated raw sessions are excluded. Rolling daily/weekly maintenance preserves permanent archive copies according to the history settings. No user archives or migration scripts are included in this public package.

CI runs portable memory-indexing and recall tests using `npm test`. The full plugin integration suite (`npm run test:integration`) requires a compatible DSH host with the declared peer services.

## Requirements and install

Requires a DSH host with native session query, scheduling and model services; see [package.json](package.json) for runtime and peer requirements.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Kerberos255/dsh-memory-dreaming
```

Use your actual profile and restart after installing or updating code.

## Quick start

1. Open **Settings → Plugins → Dream & Memory**. Choose an available summarization model.
2. Start with the manual daily/Dream/weekly actions and inspect eligible-source diagnostics and proposed facts.
3. Review the candidate list and publish verified facts, or deliberately enable automatic promotion with its evidence checks.
4. Enable the built-in DSH scheduled jobs only when wanted; **scheduled processing and automatic fact promotion are off by default**.
5. For private Discord/Feishu sources, configure [Channel Core](https://github.com/Kerberos255/dsh-channel-core) owner verification first.

By default, published facts can be recalled automatically in small bounded amounts. The plugin supports keyword retrieval without an embedding model; an optional embedding provider may improve semantic matching.

## Storage and safety

State and write recovery are managed in local SQLite under DSH data; managed journals, Dream output and `MEMORY.md` remain regular workspace Markdown. Source identity, workspace authorization, incremental cursors, atomic writes, and hash checks protect publication and cleanup. Archived eligible daily entries are retained temporarily before removal; human-edited files are preserved.

An on-demand `memory_dream` tool is **not** permission to inspect unrelated private conversations. Live model and scheduling results must be checked in DSH; standalone CI covers mock-based behavior.

## Development

Run `npm test` for portable tests. Config template: [config.example.json](config.example.json). Historical changes: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

Related: [Channel Core](https://github.com/Kerberos255/dsh-channel-core) · [Instruction Files](https://github.com/Kerberos255/dsh-instruction-files) · [Lossless Context](https://github.com/Kerberos255/dsh-lossless-context).

MIT licensed. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

## Optional plugin diagnostics

The plugin optionally emits privacy-restricted operation and failure metadata to dsh-plugin-diagnostics. Diagnostics contain event type, status, fixed error code and elapsed time; conversation content and credentials are not logged. The diagnostics plugin is optional and does not change the host requirements.

## Natural-language project and task memory

Dream can extract source-backed task events from eligible user messages and link them to stable internal task/project IDs without requiring users to type canonical names. State changes (requested, in progress, blocked, completed, cancelled, reopened) are stored separately from verified long-term facts, with timestamps and verbatim source references. Unclear aliases remain separate rather than being forcibly merged. A status question can receive a dated task timeline via `memory_search` and limited owner-authorized recall; historical user statements are **not evidence of verified implementation**. Manual draft-only runs do not publish events, and revoked/forgotten sources are excluded.

Daily, Dream and weekly consolidation now offer distinct configurable default content-guidance prompts, with a **Restore default** action in the plugin settings. Mandatory JSON, authorization and source verification remain code-enforced. Existing native DSH Session Log remains the evidence source. The task index is populated on new successful memory runs; older journals are still searchable but are not automatically backfilled into structured tasks.

## Optional scheduled-task failure event

After a scheduled memory-maintenance workflow's failure is recorded durably, Dream emits a small `dsh/task-alert` host event with the workflow ID, kind and failed state. Manual runs, successful runs and runs with no new material do not emit an alert. Channel Core, when separately installed and opted in through its task-notification settings, can deliver a brief notification to the verified owner's Feishu or Discord DM. Dream has **no dependency on Channel Core**, and task execution never fails because notifications are unavailable. The event contains no private conversation, memory artifact, or model error detail; notifications are not guaranteed while the host is stopped.

plugins.description: Choose your own configured model and reasoning effort for DeepSeek Harness Auto Review.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH-Custom-Auto-Review

Configure a separate DSH model route to review tool calls before execution.

简体中文 · Maintenance policy

DSH-Custom-Auto-Review adds a configurable review gate for DSH tool calls. The reviewer route is selected independently from the main model route. The review request still contains session and tool-call information, so a separate route does not create an isolated context or a privacy boundary. Package: `@local/dsh-custom-auto-review@0.3.0`. Install a versioned `.tgz` from this repository's GitHub Releases. The package is not published as an npm registry package. ## What it does - Uses a user-selected, already configured DSH model provider and model for review. - Reviews supported native tool calls and started PTC inner calls before their tool bodies run. - Fails closed when review cannot complete; it does not fall back to the main model. - Keeps review-model settings separate from the main-model selection. Model-based review is probabilistic. It is not a security guarantee and must not replace DSH permission controls or human review for sensitive operations. ## Compatibility | DSH version | Support status | | --- | --- | | `0.2.1-rc.1` | In the tested compatibility scope | | `0.2.1-rc.2` | In the tested compatibility scope; primary target for this maintenance round | | Other versions | Not verified; no compatibility claim | The package requires Node.js `>=24`. The automated suite passed 134 tests on each of `0.2.1-rc.1` and `0.2.1-rc.2`. These results do not establish GUI interaction or live-provider acceptance, which require user confirmation. ## Install or roll back 1. Open the [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/QR-0W/DSH-Custom-Auto-Review/releases) page and select the exact release tag. 2. Download that release's `.tgz` asset and install the local archive through DSH Plugin Manager. Confirm the installed package version and follow the result shown by the manager. 3. To roll back, choose a prior release tag and install its matching `.tgz` through the same manager. Do not install a floating or unpinned package. Use one release artifact at a time. Follow the selected release's migration notes and verify the active review provider before enabling Auto. ## Configure the reviewer 1. Configure a model provider in DSH first. This plugin does not include a model service or supply model access. 2. Open the plugin's settings form. The initial reviewer route is empty; choose a registered provider and model, then select a reasoning effort supported by that model when available. 3. Save the reviewer settings explicitly. Saving does not change the main model and does not select or enable Auto. 4. Select Auto separately only after checking the route, review behavior, and permission policy. The plugin never silently inherits or falls back to the main model. Without a valid reviewer route, review is unavailable and tool execution remains blocked by the gate. There is no free-model or hosted-service promise. ## Privacy and safety For a review request, the plugin sends the selected reviewer the working directory, project instructions, filtered session history, and the pending tool-call details needed for the decision. These inputs can contain private project information. Review-route separation is a configuration choice, not context isolation or data redaction. Use a provider approved for the data in the session, and do not include secrets in test prompts or public examples. A reviewer denial can still be subject to DSH's configured human-approval policy. A failed, timed-out, cancelled, or invalid review does not authorize the pending tool body. Keep DSH permission guards enabled and treat model output as fallible. ## Development The following commands are the repository's current development scripts. `npm run link:runtime` links the exact DSH APIs used by the test harness; it does not install another runtime. See [maintenance policy](docs/MAINTENANCE.md) for the version-specific checks and release process. ```sh npm run link:runtime npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefix tools/gui/build-tools npm run build:gui npm run check ``` Do not use a live model gateway as a routine test target. Live-provider checks require explicit authorization and must use synthetic, non-sensitive input. ## Attribution and license This project includes source from DeepSeek's [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-auto-review`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) version `0.2.1-rc.1`, licensed under MIT. This project adds a separately configurable reviewer route and settings UI. See [source notice](NOTICE.md), [license](LICENSE), and [maintenance policy](docs/MAINTENANCE.md). ## Links - [Source and issues](https://github.com/QR-0W/DSH-Custom-Auto-Review) - [Releases](https://github.com/QR-0W/DSH-Custom-Auto-Review/releases) - [中文说明](README.zh-CN.md) - [Maintenance policy](docs/MAINTENANCE.md)

# dsh-composer-input-history

Shell-style input history for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web composer — the behaviour you know from opencode and other terminal agents.

> Press <kbd>↑</kbd> in the composer to pull back a message you already sent in this Session.
> Press <kbd>↓</kbd> to walk forward again; past the newest message your original draft comes back,
> and one more <kbd>↓</kbd> discards it and clears the composer.

## What it does

| Gesture | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> with an empty draft | recalls the newest sent message |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> again | walks one message older each time |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> on the first line of a single-line draft | recalls; the draft you were writing is remembered |
| <kbd>↑</kbd> inside a multi-line draft, below the first line | left to the editor, so the caret still moves |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> while browsing | walks one message newer |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> past the newest message | restores the draft you were writing before browsing |
| <kbd>↓</kbd> again, after the draft came back | discards the draft and clears the composer |
| typing anything while browsing | leaves browse mode; the recalled text becomes your draft |

History is what you sent in this Session, oldest to newest, read from the Chat node store the view itself renders (`snapshot.nodes`, ordered by anchor sequence): ordinary user messages, steering messages, and the message that woke a turn. Skipped: hidden nodes (compacted or interrupted), attachment-only messages, and everything the Harness authors on your behalf — goal rounds, skill catalogs, runtime snapshots, job notices, model notices, approval answers, and compaction checkpoints. The visible window is also persisted per Session in `localStorage` (capped at 300 entries) and merged with the live store, so messages a compaction pruned stay recallable, including after a restart.

## Why it is a keyboard observer

The Harness composer deliberately leaves <kbd>↑</kbd>/<kbd>↓</kbd> to its shell-owned Lexical editor, so no slot or command seam owns them. This plugin therefore:

- registers an invisible Session-scoped occupant in `conversation.composer.dock`;
- reads the Session's Chat nodes through the standard `useChat` hook (`snapshot.nodes`) and the draft through the standard `useInput` hook;
- writes the recalled text through the standard `inputActions.setDraft` API, so the edit stays part of the composer's own draft history;
- watches the key on two paths: a document-level `keydown` listener and the shortcuts service's `observeFixedInput` seam. The document listener runs after the composer's own keymap, so a slash menu or an IME that already handled the key still wins; the fixed-input seam covers compositions where a native Desktop adapter owns the DOM feed. Exactly one path acts, because the first one to act cancels the event.

Replacing a draft commits paragraph by paragraph, so intermediate empty or partial drafts are expected; the plugin treats a published draft that matches what it wrote (ignoring whitespace) as its own and keeps browse mode. Only a genuinely visible slash/reference menu (a mounted `role="listbox"`), an IME composition, or a held modifier keeps the key — a caret move the editor already marked as handled does not. Editing keys (Backspace, Delete, Enter, printable characters, <kbd>Ctrl+V</kbd>/<kbd>Ctrl+X</kbd>) end browse mode; navigation keys and shortcuts such as <kbd>Ctrl+C</kbd> do not. The browse state machine itself is cached per composer editor element, so re-rendering or remounting the dock entry never drops the browse state or the remembered draft, and starting browse again from an already-recalled message never overwrites the draft you were writing — walking past the newest message always lands on that draft, a blank composer included. When the host re-seeds a stale stored draft over a restore, the plugin re-asserts the restored text (the counter-punch yields only to genuine text editing, not to arrow keys), and every handled key re-arms that defense for the text it just published.

A key is declined when an open menu owns it, when an IME is composing, when a modifier is held, when the event is outside the composer editor, or when the composer is submitting/adjudicating. The plugin imports no Harness Client package and styles nothing.

## Install

From npm (short form):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-composer-input-history
```

Or straight from this repository:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/liumorrisclaw/dsh-composer-input-history
```

You can also add it in the Web UI's **Plugins** page, or list the package directory with the plugin manager. The bundle ships off until the profile selects it.

For a local checkout, install by path:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-composer-input-history
```

## Relationship to other plugins

The npm name `dsh-input-history` is already taken by a different community plugin that also recalls prompts with <kbd>↑</kbd>/<kbd>↓</kbd>. The two differ in mechanism and behaviour:

| | dsh-composer-input-history (this plugin) | dsh-input-history |
| --- | --- | --- |
| History source | the Session transcript the Chat view already loads | a separate local store of submitted prompts |
| Non-empty draft | recalls and remembers the draft, restoring it below the newest message | recalls only from an empty composer |
| Attachments | not part of the recalled text | persists and re-attaches them |
| Menu/IME | yields the key to an open slash/reference menu and to IME composition | — |

Pick this one if you want recall driven by the conversation you can see, including from a draft you are already typing.

## Compatibility

Developed and verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `0.2.0-rc.2`. The plugin uses only documented seams: `ctx.slots`, the Session standard props (`useChat`, `useInput`, `inputActions`), `ctx.shortcuts.observeFixedInput`, and the activation context's `uiSession` binding source (declared in `dsh.client.inject`). It declares `dsh.client.inject` on `dsh-client-ui-conversation`, `dsh-client-ui-chat`, and `dsh-client-shortcuts` so activation order is deterministic.

## Verified

- 48 tests (`npm test`): 40 unit tests over the pure history reader, the browse navigator, and keystroke arbitration, plus 6 simulated-composer integration tests that mount the real bundle against a stub React host and stub DOM — whole-draft publish, the stale-draft refill and its counter-punch, compaction pruning merged with the persistent record, manual edits, menu yields, and IME declines.
- The composed profile contains the bundle row (`dsh --profile <name> --dump-config`).
- The browser boot graph announces the bundle with its inject list and `immediately: true`, and the web host serves the bundle body byte-for-byte.
- End-to-end in a real harness Web instance driven over the DevTools protocol: the dock entry mounts in a session composer, <kbd>↑</kbd> recalls the sent message, walking down lands on the draft and a further <kbd>↓</kbd> clears it, a typed draft survives rapid up/down walks, and the console stays clean.
- Recalling a message with <kbd>↑</kbd> was confirmed by hand in a running Desktop composer.

## Limitations

- History is per Session. Cross-session recall (recent Sessions' inputs) is not implemented yet.
- History reflects the loaded transcript window plus the persisted per-Session record; a message never seen by this plugin (sent while it was uninstalled) is not recalled.
- The recalled text is plain text: reference chips and attachments from the original message are not restored.
- One resident composer per Web page is assumed, matching the shell's own design.
- On the home screen (no Session open) there is no recall: the composer dock only renders inside a session.

## License

MIT

# DSH Connect MiniMax Code (`dsh-connect-minimaxcode`)

把本机已登录的 **MiniMax Code 桌面 App（国内版）** 的模型接入 **DeepSeek Harness（DSH）**，装好即用，无需配置 API Key。

![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)
[![version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-connect-minimaxcode?color=cb3837)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-connect-minimaxcode)
[![CI](https://github.com/JeffTsuiCUG/dsh-connect-minimaxcode/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/JeffTsuiCUG/dsh-connect-minimaxcode/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

[English](README.en.md) | 简体中文

## 灵感来源

本插件的思路来自 **[corrinehu/dsh-workbuddy-connect](https://github.com/corrinehu/dsh-workbuddy-connect)**（作者 Corrine Hu）。

它最早证明了这样一件事：**桌面 App 已经登录的模型，可以零配置地搬进 DSH**——不去碰账号密码，不引入新的鉴权体系，只是把本机已有的登录态接上一个 provider，并复用 DSH 自带的 provider 适配器。本插件把同一套做法用在了 MiniMax Code 上：

| | dsh-workbuddy-connect | 本插件 |
|---|---|---|
| 数据来源 | WorkBuddy 桌面 App 的本地登录态 | MiniMax Code 桌面 App 的本地登录态 |
| 接入方式 | 注册 DSH provider，暴露已登录模型 | 同左 |
| 目录来源 | 上游实时模型列表 | 同左 |

同方向的另一实现是 **[dingminhua/dsh-connect-workbuddy](https://github.com/dingminhua/dsh-connect-workbuddy)**，本插件在**插件结构与 provider 注册的组织方式**上参考了同一作者的 [dsh-connect-trae](https://github.com/dingminhua/dsh-connect-trae)（该项目的连接内核本身也参照了 corrinehu 的实现，见其 README 致谢）。

> 两者的价值可以这样区分：**corrinehu 是最早的开创者**，「复用本机登录态」的路线由它确立；**dingminhua 的实现更贴近 DSH 插件结构的既有约定**，本插件的目录布局与 `cordis.patch.yml` 写法沿用了后者。二者都已列入文末致谢。

---

## ⚠️ 重要声明（请先阅读）

- **本项目仅供学习与研究使用**，不面向生产环境，也不提供任何商业支持。
- **本项目为非官方插件**，与 MiniMax、DeepSeek 均无关联，未获其认可或授权。
- 本插件仅**读取你自己本机上 MiniMax Code 已登录的凭证**，仅驱动**你自己的账号在你自己的电脑上**调用。
- **禁止**将本插件用于商业用途、超出个人合理使用范围的场景，或任何批量/多账号/规避限额的目的。
- 本插件依赖 MiniMax 客户端的**非公开接口**。MiniMax 更新客户端后，接口可能变更导致插件失效。
- 使用者需自行遵守 [MiniMax 的服务条款](https://agent.minimax.cn/doc/zh/terms-of-service.html)。因使用本插件产生的一切后果（账号受限、额度清空、服务中断等）由使用者自行承担。
- 本项目作者不对任何因使用或不当使用本插件造成的直接或间接损失负责。

---

## 特点

- **零配置**：自动读取 MiniMax Code 桌面 App 的登录态，不在 DSH 中存储任何明文 Token
- **动态模型目录**：从上游接口实时拉取，模型增减无需更新插件
- **积分余额可见**：在对话框底部的胶囊里显示 MiniMax Code 的剩余积分，以及本机累计消耗
- **实时消耗统计**：每次请求的 token 用量取自上游响应本身，可按官方价目表折算等效金额
- **复用官方适配器**：上游为标准 Anthropic Messages 协议，直接复用 DSH 自带 provider，工具调用、推理块、上下文压缩均由 DSH 托管
- **只读为主**：除「续期已过期的桌面 App 登录态」外，不写入、不修改 MiniMax 的任何文件，也不执行任何登录动作
- **界面不打扰**：胶囊只在输入框下方的 dock 里占一行，不改动 DSH 的其它界面

## 前置条件

1. 已安装并**登录 MiniMax Code 桌面 App（国内版）**
2. DSH 桌面版（内置内核 `0.2.0` 系列）或 Web profile

## 安装

**方式一：从 Git 仓库安装**（推荐，拿到最新代码）

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:JeffTsuiCUG/dsh-connect-minimaxcode
```

**方式二：npm 安装**（发布后可用）

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-connect-minimaxcode
```

Web profile 把 `--profile desktop` 换成 `--profile web`。

> 桌面版的 profile 由 Electron 应用独占，若 `dsh` 命令不在 PATH 中，请使用 DSH 应用自带的载体 CLI（路径随安装位置而变，例如 `<DSH安装目录>\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd`）。

安装后**无需重启**，插件会热加载；模型随后出现在模型选择器的 **MiniMax Code** 分组中。

> 界面胶囊（积分余额）属于浏览器侧插件，**首次安装或升级到 0.3.0 后需要重启一次 DSH** 才会出现在输入框下方。

### 若安装被 `allowBuilds` 拦截

本仓库把构建产物 `lib/` 一并提交，因此正常情况下安装不会触发构建。若你看到：

```text
[ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED] Failed to prepare git-hosted package
```

说明你使用的是**某个早于 `0.2.1` 的提交**（那些版本尚未提交 `lib/`）。解决办法二选一：

- 改用上面写法指定版本：`github:JeffTsuiCUG/dsh-connect-minimaxcode#v0.2.1`
- 或在该 profile 的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 中加入 pnpm 提示的 `allowBuilds` 条目后重试

## 使用流程

1. **确认桌面 App 已登录**
   打开 MiniMax Code 桌面 App，确认处于已登录状态。插件读取的是 App 写入的本地登录态。

2. **安装插件**（见上一步的命令），等待热加载完成。

3. **选择模型**
   打开 DSH 的模型选择器，在 **MiniMax Code** 分组下选择模型。可用模型来自上游实时目录，例如 `M3`、`M3.1-Flash`。

4. **正常对话**
   直接使用即可。工具调用由 DSH 本地工具执行，插件只负责提供模型通路。

5. **令牌过期时重新登录**
   MiniMax Code 有**两份互不通用**的登录态，本插件各用其一：

   | 凭证 | 位置 | 有效期 | 用途 |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | JWT | `~/.minimax/local-runtime.auth.json` | 约 15 天 | 调模型网关（`/mavis/api/v1/llm/v1/messages`） |
   | OAuth（`mmoat_`） | `~/.minimax/auth/prod/<region>/mcode-public/auth.json` | 约 1 小时 | 读账户与积分（`/matrix/api/v1/commerce/get_membership_info`） |

   两份凭证互不通用：拿 JWT 打账户接口一律 `401`，拿 OAuth 令牌打模型网关同样不通。**模型对话**用 JWT，**积分显示**用 OAuth。

   | 现象 | 含义 | 处理方式 |
   |---|---|---|
   | 正常使用 | 两份凭证都有效 | — |
   | 模型报鉴权错误 | JWT 已失效 | 在 MiniMax Code 中**重新登录**，然后重启 DSH |
   | 积分胶囊显示「登录态已过期」 | OAuth 令牌过期 | 插件会用 App 自己的 refresh token 续期并写回；若续期失败，请打开一次 MiniMax Code 桌面 App 让它自行续期 |

   > OAuth 令牌过期**不会**影响模型对话：JWT 仍然有效，模型照常可用，只是积分胶囊暂时拿不到余额。
   >
   > 续期会**轮换** refresh token。插件因此把新的一对令牌按客户端**原格式原子写回**同一个文件，并保持 `generation` 不变——客户端靠它判断「这份凭据是否仍属于本次登录」，擅自抬高会让桌面 App 误判为异地登录。

### 关于响应速度

MiniMax 的这些模型**强制要求先推理再输出**，思考无法关闭。因此：

- 首个字符出现前会有一段等待（实测 M3.1-Flash 约 3 秒）
- 推理过程会以 `thinking` 块实时返回，可以在界面中看到模型"在想什么"
- 这是模型本身的行为，**不是插件造成的延迟**

若更看重流式体感的即时反馈，建议同时保留 DSH 官方模型或其他 provider 作为备选。

## 工作原理

1. 读取 `~/.minimax/local-runtime.auth.json`（MiniMax Code 写入的明文登录信息），**仅在内存中**解析其 JWT
2. 调用 `GET /mavis/api/v1/models` 获取实时模型目录（含上下文长度、多模态、工具调用等能力声明）
3. 注册 `minimaxcode` provider，指向 `POST /mavis/api/v1/llm/v1/messages`（标准 Anthropic Messages 协议）
4. 读取 `~/.minimax/auth/prod/<region>/mcode-public/auth.json` 的 OAuth 令牌，按需续期
5. 调用 `POST /matrix/api/v1/commerce/get_membership_info` 获取积分余额，通过插件自己的状态接口 `/plugins/dsh-connect-minimaxcode/status` 交给界面胶囊

### 与网关对接时的三个兼容处理

这些是实测中必须处理的差异，也是本插件与"直接改个 URL 就能用"的主要差异所在：

| # | 现象 | 处理 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 网关只认 `Authorization: Bearer`，而 pi-ai 默认发 `x-api-key`，后者单独出现会返回 `401 token is required` | 在模型描述符上附带 `Authorization` 头（网关同时接受两个头） |
| 2 | Anthropic SDK 会自己在 `baseUrl` 后追加 `/v1/messages`；若 `baseUrl` 已以 `/v1` 结尾，请求路径会变成 `/v1/v1/messages`，网关返回 `503 direct_route_not_configured` | `baseUrl` 收到版本段之前，由 SDK 补齐 |
| 3 | 所有模型强制要求推理，而"关闭推理"会让 pi-ai 发出 `thinking: {type: "disabled"}`，网关返回 `400 ... requires adaptive thinking` | 将"关闭"级别标记为不支持，使该字段被省略（网关接受） |

插件**不**包含任何硬编码的 Token、账号或接口密钥。

## 积分余额与用量

对话框输入框下方的胶囊会显示 MiniMax Code 的**剩余积分**；点开还能看到赠送/购买拆分、两次读取之间的消耗，以及本机累计的 token 与等效金额。

### 余额从哪里来

MiniMax Code 桌面 App 自己每天在调一个「会员信息」接口，响应里就带着客户端设置页显示的那三个数字：

```
POST https://agent.minimax.cn/matrix/api/v1/commerce/get_membership_info
Authorization: Bearer <桌面 App 的 mmoat_ OAuth 令牌>
Content-Type: application/json

{}
```

```json
"op_credit_summary": {
  "total_remaining_amount": "11459.454",      // 总剩余积分
  "purchased_remaining_amount": "0",           // 其中购买的
  "free_remaining_amount": "11459.454"         // 其中赠送的
}
```

插件读的就是 `op_credit_summary.total_remaining_amount`。**注意别取错字段**：同一个响应里的 `total_remains_credit` 与 `opcredit_balance` 是旧账，在已迁移到积分池的账号上恒为 `0`，取它们会显示「0 积分」。

顺带一提，这里有三个**单位不同**的「钱」，别混：

| 数值 | 含义 | 本插件是否显示 |
|---|---|---|
| `op_credit_summary.total_remaining_amount` | Code 积分余额 | ✅ 就是它 |
| `token_plan_credit.remaining_credits` | 已购积分池 | ❌ |
| `query_balance.available_amount` | 开放平台钱包（元） | ❌ |

### 积分会过期吗？会

积分不是一池子，而是**按笔发放的批次**，每批有自己的到期日。客户端每天发一批，每批在**发放日 + 30 个自然日**到期（按账户所在时区，当日 00:00 失效），于是形成一条逐日错开的 30 天阶梯：

```
GET https://agent.minimax.cn/minimax-cloud/api/v1/credit/details?page_number=1&page_size=100
→ details[] { granted_amount, remaining_amount, consumed_amount, granted_at_ms, expire_at_ms, credit_type }
```

实测本机 23 笔：09-20 发的在 10-20 到期、09-21 发的在 10-21 到期……另有一笔 08-25 发的在 2027-08-25 到期（一年期批次，`credit_type` 1=购买 / 2=签到）。**到期日一律读 `expire_at_ms`**，不写死天数——至少存在 30 天与 365 天两种制式。

插件据此在**插件页面**（设置 → 插件 → DSH Connect MiniMax Code）与输入框下方的胶囊里给出：

- **7 天内到期**的剩余积分，以及最近一笔的到期日
- **30 天内到期**的剩余积分
- 接下来几笔**到期批次**的清单（日期 + 金额）
- 余额条与本机消耗（token 数、等效金额）

只统计**仍有余额**的批次：已发放但用光的批次到期时并没有东西可损失，把它算进去会让每个账号都看起来"快过期了"。积分的消耗近似先进先出，所以**"7 天内到期"的金额常常是 0**（快到期的那些基本都已被用完），因此界面同时给出**最早到期时间**，那才是真正有意义的信号。

> 过期不会把批次里的 `remaining_amount` 清零（实测会留下 -0.31 这样的负值残留），而是把过期批次**排除在余额之外**；所以总额以余额接口为准。
>
> 台账的 `remaining_amount` 合计与余额接口的 `total_remaining_amount` 在**静止期逐位相等**；两次采样之间看到的差异，是账户在这段时间里被真实消耗掉的量。

### 消耗怎么算

两路数据各管一件事：

- **真实积分消耗**：余额是个活值，两次读取的差值就是这段时间真正花掉的积分（客户端也会并发消耗，所以差值含其它客户端的开销）。
- **本机消耗**：每次请求的响应都自带 `usage`（`input_tokens` / `output_tokens` / `cache_creation_input_tokens` / `cache_read_input_tokens`），插件原样累计。折算金额时**只用这四个分量自己算**，不能用任何 `total_token` 汇总值——上游的两级汇总口径不同（差 1.94 倍，差额正是缓存读取部分）。单价取自 [MiniMax 官方价目表](https://platform.minimax.cn/docs/pricing/overview)：

  | 模型 | 输入 | 输出 | 缓存读取 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` | 1.00 元/百万

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-bid-ca-precheck — Bid document compliance pre-check against each tender requirement

[English](README.md) · [简体中文](README-zh.md) · [Español](README-es.md) · [Português](README-pt.md) · [हिन्दी](README-hi.md)

[![DSH Market](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2BingLing/dsh-market/master/assets/readme/badge-listed-en.svg)](https://dsh.market/)
[![dshfind](https://dshfind.com/api/badge/PerryLink/dsh-bid-ca-precheck?metric=downloads)](https://dshfind.com/en/plugins/PerryLink/dsh-bid-ca-precheck?ref=badge)

`dsh-bid-ca-precheck` reads one 投标符合性响应台账 — the tender's requirements and the bidder's responses, keyed by the register's own column names in Chinese or English — applies a versioned rule pack, and checks that register's own completeness and internal consistency: that every tender requirement has a recorded response, that the verdict comes from the vocabulary you configure, that clause numbers are unique within the register, that the register declares its project and its bidder, that a clause you marked high-risk carries evidence, and that the requirement column still holds real requirements rather than template placeholders.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-bid-ca-precheck
dsh --profile <name> --dump-config | grep 'dsh-bid-ca-precheck'
```

## What it looks like

![Workflow diagram for dsh-bid-ca-precheck: call → plugin → result.](docs/assets/dsh-bid-ca-precheck-flow.svg)

*Workflow overview: call → plugin → result. The examples below use the real command surface.*



## What it answers

### Examples

The table below is the example set: the first row is the detailed walkthrough, the remaining rows are short cases.

#### Detailed output

**Tool** `bid_ca_precheck`

**Input**

~~~json
{"rows":[{"条款号":"2.1","招标要求":"投标人应具有建筑工程施工总承包二级及以上资质","投标响应":"","响应结论":"满足", ...}]}
~~~
 
**Output**

~~~json
{
  "id": "dsh-bid-ca-precheck.BC-001.de09b5a6",
  "ruleId": "BC-001",
  "severity": "warn",
  "locator": {
    "row": 1,
    "field": "response"
  },
  "found": "第 1 行「response」为空",
  "expected": "「response」应填写",
  "fix": "补填响应内容；本条只核对是否填写，不判断该响应对招标要求是否构成实质性满足"
}
~~~

*Observed from `dsh-bid-ca-precheck/tests/fixtures/BC-001/BC-001-unsafe.json; dsh-bid-ca-precheck/tests/fixtures/BC-001/cases.json; dsh-bid-ca-precheck/rules/bid-ca-precheck.yaml; dsh-bid-ca-precheck/tests/index.test.ts`*

| You ask | What it answers |
|---|---|
| A tender requirement's `response` column is blank. Is that reported? | Yes. `BC-001` reports the row, because every tender requirement must have a recorded response. It only checks that the `response` column is filled — it does not judge whether the response satisfies the requirement, which is the evaluation committee's call. |
| I filled the `verdict` column and the report still says the rule could not run. Why? | `BC-002` compares each value with the verdict vocabulary you configure, and that list ships empty, so until you fill `values` the rule reports itself in `skipped` rather than guessing. Once configured it only reports a value that is not in your list; it never judges whether the verdict itself is correct. |
| The same clause number appears on two rows of the register. | `BC-003` reports the repeated `clause` value: when one number appears twice, nobody can tell which row answers which requirement. Whitespace is ignored, so `3.2` and ` 3.2 ` count as the same number. It only checks uniqueness — it does not decide which of the two rows is right; a hit usually means duplicate registration or a copied-wrong number. |
| The register does not say which project it covers or who the bidder is. | `BC-004` reports the missing header field and requires both `project` and `bidder`. That need comes from traceability — a verdict that cannot be tied to a project and a bidder cannot be reviewed later — not from a clause that requires a register header. |
| Which rows must carry evidence? | `BC-005`: every row whose `requirement` text contains one of your high-risk keywords, matched by containment. `highRiskKeywords` ships empty, so until you fill it the rule reports itself in `skipped` rather than passing silently. It only checks that the `evidence` column is filled, not whether the evidence is valid or sufficient. |
| A few rows still read 【……】 or 待填 in the requirement column. | `BC-006` reports them: `【`, `】`, `{{`, `}}`, `XXX`, `待填`, `TBD` and similar terms left in the `requirement` column usually mean the register was copied from a template and never filled in. The terms list is yours to adjust. The rule flags the placeholder only; it does not decide whether the requirement itself is real. |

## Standards it follows

| Document | Number | Cited by rules |
|---|---|---|
| 《中华人民共和国招标投标法》 | 1999年8月30日通过，2017年12月27日修正（全国人大常委会《关于修改〈中华人民共和国招标投标法〉、〈中华人民共和国计量法〉的决定》），本法自2000年1月1日起施行 | BC-001, BC-003, BC-004, BC-006 |
| 《中华人民共和国招标投标法实施条例》 | 国务院令第613号（2011 年 12 月 20 日公布，2017 年 3 月 1 日修订，自 2012 年 2 月 1 日起施行） | BC-002 |
| 《中华人民共和国招标投标法》 | 1999年8月30日通过，2017年12月27日修正，自2000年1月1日起施行 | BC-005 |

**Boundary:** this plugin checks a **投标符合性响应台账** for what a register can be held to — that every
tender requirement has a recorded response, that verdicts come from your vocabulary and clause numbers are
unique, that a high-risk clause carries evidence, and that the requirement column still holds real
requirements rather than template placeholders. It does **not** decide whether a bid is valid, whether it
should be rejected, or whether a response is a material deviation. **Those calls belong to the evaluation
committee, and this plugin never makes them** — a test asserts that no rule here can be `error`.

> ### ⚠️ Read this before trusting a citation in the report
>
> **Every `excerpt` in this plugin's rule pack says, in so many words, that the clause text was not
> obtained.** The regime lives in 《招标投标法》, 《招标投标法实施条例》 and each project's 评标办法. The
> verification pass for this plugin could not retrieve verbatim clause text from them, so rather than
> paraphrase a quotation the pack states the gap in the `excerpt` field itself and puts the honest
> reasoning in `note`. Every rule is therefore `warn` or `info`, and a test asserts that no rule claims a
> quotation it does not have. **When the texts are in hand, two things must be done: replace each
> `excerpt` with the real clause, and raise `kind` to `direct`.**
>
> The worst failure mode of a register tool is a register copied from a template and mistaken for a
> checked one, so `BC-006` looks for exactly that: `【】`, `{{}}`, `XXX`, `待填`, `TBD` left in the
> requirement column.
>
> Two lists are yours, not a standard's: the verdict vocabulary (`BC-002`) and the high-risk keywords
> (`BC-005`). Both ship **empty**, and a rule whose list is unset reports itself in `skipped` rather than
> passing silently.

## Compatibility

| Surface | Status |
|---|---|
| Harness | Peer range `>=0.1.2-rc.1 <0.2.0 \|\| >=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0` — verified to accept both `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.1-rc.2`. `engines.dsh` is declared as `>=0.2.1-0 <0.3.0` and is enforced by the host since 0.2.1 |
| Node | `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` |
| Platforms | All (plain ESM; no native code, no network, no model call) |
| Tool mode | Works in `native` and `ptc`; for a batch of registers use `ptc` |

## What it does

Registers the `bid_ca_precheck` tool. It reads one compliance register — the tender's requirements and the
bidder's responses, keyed by the register's own column names in Chinese or English — applies a versioned
rule pack, and returns a report.

| Rule | Check | Severity | Basis kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BC-001` | every requirement has a recorded response | warn | direct |
| `BC-002` | the verdict uses your vocabulary (off by default) | info | local |
| `BC-003` | clause numbers are unique in the register | warn | principle |
| `BC-004` | the register names its project and its bidder | warn | principle |
| `BC-005` | a high-risk clause carries evidence (off by default) | warn | direct |
| `BC-006` | the requirement column holds no unreplaced placeholder | warn | principle |
## Configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rulesFile` | string | `rules/bid-ca-precheck.yaml` | Rule-pack path, r

plugins.description: DSH plugin: colors sidebar session rows by their official status in an Evangelion-flavored palette - orange = pending interaction, red = selected session, purple = finished but unviewed, rainbow title = pinned.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-session-eva-status

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Colors DSH sidebar Session rows by their **official** UI status, in an Evangelion-flavored palette. The plugin owns no state: it reads facts the Client already has, writes one `data-` attribute per row, and styles that attribute from a single injected stylesheet.

| Row state | Official fact it reads | Decoration |
|---|---|---|
| Pending interaction (approval / question / plan review) | `uiSession.sessionStatus.pendingInteraction` | blue full-height left rail + 1.6 s breathing. Two blues, one per mode, both from card C ("Newtype" cover): dark `#AAC7EF`, light `#3F629C` |
| Selected — the session open in the main view | `sessions.list` snapshot: `retainedBy.mainView > 0` | red full-height left rail, static. Two reds, one per mode: dark keeps `#FF3B30`, light overrides it with the redder, deeper `#E01B24` |
| Finished but not viewed | `…sessionStatus.completionUnread` | purple `#7A4FD6` full-height left rail |
| Pinned | `workspaces.list` snapshot: `pinnedSessionIds` | the row title becomes a static six-color rainbow (`background-clip: text`); the row itself gets no rail. Two palettes, one per mode: dark keeps the original six, light uses a darker six solved to ≥4.5:1 against the light wall |
| Running / subagents running / idle / archived / blank | — | nothing drawn; the official spinner and archived dimming already say it |

The official priority is pending > running > subagents > completed. When a session has finished but its subagents are still running, the official row shows the ongoing spinner, so this plugin draws nothing and lets that spinner through instead of calling the row "finished".

The plugin's own priority is pending > selected > subagents (yields) > unread. A row that needs you outranks the row you happen to be looking at, and a selected row keeps its red rail while its subagents run — the official spinner is not hidden on selected rows, so both readings stay visible at once.

The design rule behind the palette: **shape carries meaning, color and light carry style.** The pin icon and the pinned-first ordering stay entirely official — only the pinned row's title text is re-colored, so the pin itself is never restyled or decorated.

The rainbow is mode-scoped, because the same mid-luminance stops do not survive both backgrounds: on the light theme's wall (measured luminance 0.405–0.658 under the pinned titles) the original six score only 1.15–3.63:1, while on the dark theme's wall they are fine. Dark therefore keeps the original six colours unchanged, and light uses six darker stops of the same hues in the same order, each clearing 4.5:1 against the darkest patch measured under the title. The split is read from DSH's own dark marker (`body[data-ds-dark-theme]`, `theme-presenter.ts`), not from any theme-specific hook.

The pending rail is mode-scoped for the same reason. Its blue comes from card C (the "Newtype" cover reference), which carries two blues: `#3F629C` (slate blue — 5.84:1 on the light wall but only 2.82:1 on the dark one) and `#AAC7EF` (pale blue — 9.94:1 on the dark wall but only 1.66:1 on the light one). Neither survives both, so each mode takes the one that reads on its own wall: light `#3F629C`, dark `#AAC7EF`. Both tiers share one `@keyframes`: the rail reads its colour through a custom property (`--dsh-session-eva-status-pending`), and the light rule overrides only that property, so the breathing period, easing and low point stay byte-for-byte identical and only the colour changes.

The selected rail is mode-scoped for the same reason. `#FF3B30` keeps a high green channel (59) and scores only 3.39:1 on the light wall; light overrides the colour alone with the redder, deeper `#E01B24` — hue rotated past pure red (HSL 357.3°), green cut from 59 to 27 — which clears 4.62:1. Dark is byte-for-byte unchanged. The override is one extra rule scoped by `body:not([data-ds-dark-theme])` that sets `background` and nothing else, so the rail's geometry, stacking and lack of animation are untouched.

## Install

The plugin is a Profile dependency, like the other local plugins in this directory. Add it to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json` (and to that profile's `dsh.bundles` list) and restart DSH, or use the plugin CLI with the package path:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add <path-to>/dsh-session-eva-status
```

## Config

The shipped `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the entry with these defaults; edit them there.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `hideOfficialDot` | `true` | Hide the official status dot on pending and unread rows (their left rail replaces it) |
| `breatheMs` | `1600` | Breathing period for the pending rail (ms, ≥ 200) |
| `colors` | EVA palette | Override `pending` / `pendingLight` / `selected` / `selectedLight` / `unread`. `pending` and `selected` are the dark-mode values; `pendingLight` and `selectedLight` are the light-mode overrides |

A malformed config throws at load; nothing is silently skipped.

## How it works

- **Row anchor**: `[data-row-key="session:<id>"]` — rendered by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace`.
- **Title anchor**: the pinned rainbow is applied to the row's **second child**. The leading 16 px cell is always rendered, so the title's position in the row is stable and no hashed CSS-module class name has to be matched.
- **Status source**: `ctx.uiSession.sessionStatus`, the Client's own `HostObservable<ReadonlyMap<SessionId, SessionStatus>>` (`running`, `pendingInteraction`, `completionUnread`), plus `ctx.sessions.list` for two more official facts: the subagent catalog that decides the official "subagents running" state, and `retainedBy.mainView > 0` — the same fact the official row's own `selected` flag is computed from. The pinned set comes from `ctx.workspaces.list` (`pinnedSessionIds`). No polling, no event sniffing, no host half.
- **Row paint**: the state is carried by a single `::before` pseudo-element rail, and the row's own background is left completely alone — so official hover and selection feedback is untouched. The rail is deliberately **not** an `inset box-shadow`: an inset shadow is a band hugging the border's inner edge, so it follows the row's own `border-radius` all the way around and curls into a right-facing hook at each end — it reads as a bracket, not a rail. An absolutely positioned pseudo-element is not clipped by the row's radius, so the rail is one straight, square-ended bar spanning the full row height.
- **React-safe**: the marker is a `data-eva-state` attribute React does not manage, so re-renders cannot wipe it; a `MutationObserver` filtered to `data-row-key` re-reconciles when rows mount, unmount or change identity.
- **Uninstall is clean**: subscriptions, observer, row attributes, stylesheet and the debug handle all go away with the plugin fiber.

## Credits and prior art

Nothing here was copied wholesale. This list states exactly what each source contributed.

**Code techniques borrowed**

- [enterhalf/dsh-session-colorful-unread-pin-jobs](https://github.com/enterhalf/dsh-session-colorful-unread-pin-jobs) — the browser-half shape for a DSH Web plugin: the `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` envelope with named `apply` / `inject`, decorating Session rows through `[data-row-key^="session:"]`, re-applying after React re-renders with a `MutationObserver` coalesced into one microtask, and pre-tagging the injected stylesheet (`dataset.plugin` / `dataset.pluginCss`) so a sibling plugin's hot reload cannot claim and delete it. Its 2-second polling, its own unread store and its title-gradient painting were deliberately **not** reused.
- `dsh-ledger-cn` (the local plugin package in `C:\DSH\plugins\dsh-ledger-cn`, unpublished) — the package layout this plugin follows: `private: true`, `main: lib/index.js`, the `.` / `./client` export pair, a `cordis.patch.yml` that inserts its own Loader row, and the test style of loading the browser bundle behind a fake `window.__ModuleLoader__` with a minimal DOM stub.
- [Tencent/BrowserSkill — `@wxg-prc-cpg/browser-skill-dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/Tencent/BrowserSkill/tree/main/packages/dsh-plugin-browserskill) — the reference

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness 插件：看时机的优雅暂停 —— 峰时提醒（15 秒窗口）、余额不足优雅降级停机、看门狗自动唤醒续跑。人机双交接，日志全留痕 | Graceful pause on timing for DSH
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-tide

[![DSH Market](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2BingLing/dsh-market/master/assets/readme/badge-listed-zh.svg)](https://dsh.market/)

> DeepSeek Harness 插件：**看时机的优雅暂停（Graceful Pause on Timing）**。
> 退潮时暂停，涨潮时回来 —— 在"时机不对"的时刻，让 agent 优雅地把项目停在安全点、
> 留下可继承的交接，而不是硬停或继续烧钱。

## 两条链路（同一套骨架：暂停 → 双交接 → 条件唤醒）

**Part 1 · 峰时提醒（温和事件：给你选择权）**
- 谷→峰切换（"梁文谷"转"梁文峰"）时，向**最近活跃的会话**注入一条用户可见提醒：
  "在 15 秒内回复「暂停」可优雅收尾（先留交接，等便宜时段再继续）；不回复则照常推进。"
- 回复「暂停」→ 进入收尾：模型写两份交接（**人一份 + 模型一份**）→ 调用
  `submit_pause_handoff` 落盘 → 会话进入「已暂停」。
- **超时默认继续**：有些项目"宁愿多花钱、不能停"——15 秒是"抓在场的人"的窗口，
  不是等你做决定的窗口。设计上这是"同意机制"，不是"省钱强制"。
- Never Ask 模式下静默跳过（不打扰）。

**Part 2 · 余额降级（危险事件：强制处理）**
- 余额 ≤ `lowBalanceCNY` → 向活跃会话注入降级收尾指令（**不需要用户同意**），
  模型写双交接后停下。
- **看门狗**：暂停后按 `watchdogSeconds`（默认 15 分钟）轮询余额；恢复到
  `resumeBalanceCNY` 以上 → **自动唤醒模型**继续任务（模型交接原文随唤醒消息注入）。
- 未达恢复线则保持暂停，不重复打扰。

## 工作机制（全部使用公开 API，已在本机 DSH 源码逐项验证）

| 环节 | 机制 |
|---|---|
| 时间驱动 | 宿主 `setInterval` tick（默认 10s）；峰谷为北京时间周一至五 09:00–12:00、14:00–18:00（`peakWindows` 可覆盖，支持 `leadMinutes` 提前量） |
| 注入提醒/审计 | `session.append('user/message', msg, { surfaceOp: 'append' })` —— `surfaceOp` 在**回合外上下文是必须的**（surface 契约），审计元数据在 `source.tide` 字段 |
| 唤醒模型 | `ctx.sessionController.resolveAgent(sid)` → `agent.followup(message)` → `ctx.sessions.flush()`（与 dsh-schedule 同款用法） |
| 收尾产物 | `submit_pause_handoff` 工具：human 交接写工作目录 `TIDE-PAUSED-handoff.md`（+归档），model 交接写 `$DSH_HOME/storages/dsh-tide/handoffs/<会话>.md` 并随唤醒注入 |
| 余额 | 官方 `GET {baseUrl}/user/balance`（Bearer，key 走 `ctx.credentials` → 环境变量兜底），免费不耗额度 |
| 状态 | 内存状态机 + 落盘 `state.json`（暂停项跨重启）；问询窗口/暂停标记可从**会话日志重建**（跨进程可用） |

## 安装

**GitHub 直装（推荐，国内网络可直连，无需 npm 账号）**：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add 'https://codeload.github.com/wobenshiwomu/dsh-tide/tar.gz/v0.1.0'
```

或在图形界面：侧栏「插件」→ 添加插件 → 填上面这条 URL。装完重启 DSH 生效。
URL 末段的 `v0.1.0` 是版本标签；升级时换成本仓库的新版本标签重装即可。

**无需配置，开箱即用**：装好即生效——内置峰时窗口（周一至五 09:00–12:00 / 14:00–18:00，北京时间）、
余额降级（触发线 ¥5 / 恢复线 ¥20）、看门狗每 15 分钟自动巡查。不写任何配置就是这套默认行为；
下面的配置全部可选，只想自定义行为时才需要。

**本地/开发安装**（本机路径）：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-tide
```

**可选配置**（profile 用户层 `cordis.patch.yml`，覆盖构建默认；不配置即用默认值）：

```yaml
# 示例：仅当要改默认值（触发线 5 / 恢复线 20）时才需要
- id: dsh-tide
  config:
    lowBalanceCNY: 1        # 低余额触发线（元）
    resumeBalanceCNY: 3     # 余额恢复线（元，须大于触发线）
    # peakWindows: ['1-5 09:00-12:00', '1-5 14:00-18:00']
    # leadMinutes: 0        # 峰时提醒提前量（分钟）
    # askTimeoutSeconds: 15 # 提醒时效
    # watchdogSeconds: 900  # 看门狗轮询间隔
```

> ⚠️ 触发线必须小于恢复线（`low < resume`）；相等或倒置会形成"唤醒后立刻再暂停"循环，
> 启动时会打印配置提醒。

## 配置项（全量 · 全部可选，不配置即取默认）

| 键 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `askEnabled` | `true` | 峰时提醒总开关 |
| `peakWindows` | 周一至五 09:00–12:00 / 14:00–18:00 | 峰段（北京时间），格式 `"<0-6/*> <HH:MM>-<HH:MM>"` |
| `leadMinutes` | `0` | 峰时提醒提前量 |
| `askTimeoutSeconds` | `15` | 提醒中承诺的回复窗口 |
| `askValidMinutes` | `10` | 窗口后仍有效的答复时限（超过视为继续） |
| `guardWhileWrapping` | `true` | 收尾期间拦下"开新战线"工具（`denyPattern`） |
| `denyPattern` | `job_\|create_goal\|update_goal\|todo_write\|send_message\|subagent\|workflow\|ralph` | 收尾期拦截正则 |
| `activeWindowMinutes` | `720` | 只提醒最近活跃过的会话 |
| `balanceEnabled` | `true` | 余额降级总开关 |
| `lowBalanceCNY` | `5` | 低余额触发线（≤ 即触发） |
| `resumeBalanceCNY` | `20` | 恢复线（> 即唤醒） |
| `balancePollSeconds` | `60` | 常规余额轮询间隔 |
| `watchdogSeconds` | `900` | 暂停后的看门狗间隔 |
| `balanceBaseUrl` | `https://api.deepseek.com` | 余额接口 base |
| `apiKeyRef` | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | 凭据服务引用名 |
| `tickSeconds` | `10` | 宿主 tick 间隔 |
| `storageDir` | `$DSH_HOME/storages/dsh-tide` | 状态与模型交接目录 |
| `debugSeedSessions` | `[]` | 调试：预置为"已追踪"的会话 ID |

## 审计（都在会话日志里，`source.tide` 字段）

`subtype`: `ask`（峰时提醒）· `consent`（用户同意）· `decline`（继续）· `expired`（过期）·
`wrap`（收尾指令）· `paused`（已暂停，含双交接路径）· `woken`（看门狗唤醒）· `resumed`（手动恢复）。

## 已知边界

- **节假日不建模**：官方峰段不含法定节假日；本插件按"周一至五"计算（节假日白天会按峰处理，
  偏差方向保守——最多多提醒一次）。
- **`resolveAgent` 会接管会话**：提醒送到哪个会话，该会话的写句柄就属于当前实例；
  多实例（web + headless 同时）共用同一会话时会出现锁冲突——单实例使用无影响。
- **不采用原生 `ask_user_question`**：其 timed 模式非宿主默认，且设置项所在的嵌套行
  无法被用户层 patch 覆盖（实测）；本插件的非阻塞提醒方案不依赖任何 ask 模式，
  headless 环境行为一致。
- 收尾质量取决于模型；`submit_pause_handoff` 是兜底（未调用则不会标记"已暂停"）。
- 与 `dsh-calm` 架构同源（pre-step 注入 + 工具闸门），可共存。

## 测试

```sh
npm install   # 首次：安装测试所需的宿主依赖
npm test      # 仿真测试：89 项断言（时钟/窗口/同意/双交接/看门狗/跨重启/跨进程）
```

# dsh-plugin-dev-mpff

## 这是什么

一个给「dsh（DeepSeek Harness）第三方插件作者」用的 skill —— 覆盖从零写出一个插件、证明它真的生效、把它发出去的全过程。

## 覆盖什么（任务清单）

- **找 CLI / 安装根 / Node / profile** —— 先确认这台机器上的 dsh 环境在哪，再动手
- **写 manifest 与 patch** —— `package.json` 的 `dsh` 块、bundle patch 与层序
- **挑扩展点** —— 决定挂工具流水线、前端槽位还是事件
- **从零建包** —— 逐文件写出一个能跑的插件包
- **写前端半边** —— `dsh.client` 与 `client.js`
- **验证真的生效** —— 装上、mount、卸干净，每一步都有判据
- **发布与兼容性声明** —— 发到 npm 时要说清的兼容性面
- **排查静默失效** —— 插件装上了却什么都不做，从哪开始查
- **升级后重新核对** —— dsh 升级之后，哪些事实必须重新确认
- **把 skill 随包发出去** —— 让包里的 skill 真的被宿主发现，而不是装上了却静默不可见

## 边界在哪（不覆盖什么）

- 不覆盖「使用或配置一个已装插件」—— 那是使用者的事，不是作者的事
- 不覆盖「改 shipped preset」—— 官方发行版自带的组合不在第三方扩展点里
- 不覆盖「dsh 宿主本身开发」—— 宿主主循环与官方自带插件不在范围内
- 不覆盖「安装或放置这个 skill 本身」—— 落点与优先级由宿主自己的 skill 发现规则决定，本仓库不定义落点，只给一个照做用的示例
- 不覆盖「版本与变更历史」—— 本仓只有一处版本面：GitHub Releases 的 tag（不写当前版本号、不列变更历史，版本与变更都从那里读）
- 不覆盖「副本对齐」—— 取用者手上的目录束与仓库之间没有可比版本面（按 clone 取用的自带 `refs/tags`，是已知例外）

## 怎么被触发

本 skill 靠 frontmatter 的 `description` 被模型发现与触发：读者不必记路径，说清「我在写 / 装 / 发 / 查一个 dsh 插件」就够了。

- **触发面**（`description` 里的中文触发词）：dsh 插件开发、新建插件、插件包骨架、bundle patch、cordis.patch.yml、cordis 组合、宿主插件、client manifest、前端/UI 插件、扩展点选择、本地安装与验证、npm 发布、插件静默失效排查
- **排除面**（`description` 的 `Do not use for …` 一段）：使用或配置一个已装插件、改 shipped preset、dsh 宿主本身开发

`description` 是触发词与排除面的唯一真源，本节只是它的索引。被触发之后，`SKILL.md` 是唯一入口：路由表与 5 步流程在那里，其余内容（10 册分册、两套模板、闭环夹具、脚本）按需加载。

## 目录结构

取用 = 把 `dsh-plugin-dev-mpff/` 这一层整个拿走（连同 `references/`、`templates/`、`examples/`、`scripts/`）；落点与优先级由你的宿主的 skill 发现规则决定。

落点 = 把 `dsh-plugin-dev-mpff/` 这一层**整层**放进任一被扫描根的顶层，即 `<root>/dsh-plugin-dev-mpff/SKILL.md`。最省事的是**项目级根** `<projectRoot>/.dsh/skills/`（= 你的会话工作区向上最近含 `.git` 的祖先，没有就是会话目录本身；**不是**你刚 clone 下来的这个仓），不想动任何既有 profile 就用它；跨项目常驻则用**用户级根** `<dshHome>/skills/`。根按优先级排序，同名时高优先者胜（宿主文档里叫 rank，数字随宿主版本可能变，以宿主文档为准）。

完整根表与优先级（还有平铺形态 `<name>.md`）见你宿主自带的 skill 发现文档：dsh 的 skill 提供方包（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem`）的「根目录与优先级」一节。
